title: Vacuum cleaving of superconducting niobium tips for scanning tunneling microscopy
author: Marques, Cahlík, et al.

steps.title: Cut and notch Nb wire
steps.instruction: Cut a 99.9 % pure Nb wire (0.125 mm diameter) to a length of about 2 cm, tie a loop knot at the far end, insert the wire onto a tip holder, and score a shallow notch with a sharp blade at an angle of ~45° located 3 mm from the edge of the tip holder; the notch depth must be less than 50 % of the wire thickness but deep enough to create the weakest point.

steps.title: Glue wire to holder
steps.instruction: Apply conductive silver epoxy (EPOTEK 20E) to secure the wire to the tip holder and to the loop knot; cure the epoxy for 90 min at 150 °C.

steps.title: Transfer assembly to UHV
steps.instruction: Load the glued Nb‑wire assembly through the load‑lock into the preparation chamber and then into the STM chamber, which must be at a base pressure better than 3 × 10⁻¹⁰ mbar.

steps.title: In‑situ cleave Nb tip
steps.instruction: Using a wobble‑stick, grasp the loop and pull it apart; the wire will break cleanly at the pre‑made notch, leaving a fresh Nb apex ready for STM use.

steps.title: Install cleaved tip
steps.instruction: Transfer the freshly cleaved tip into the STM head and secure it in a tip‑storage slot.

steps.title: Coarse align tip on Au(111)
steps.instruction: Use the reflection of the Nb tip on a polished Au(111) surface for coarse alignment, then approach the surface (setpoint Vs = 10 mV, Is = 1.2 nA) to verify tip sharpness.

steps.title: Measure superconducting gap
steps.instruction: Acquire differential conductance spectra with Vs = 10 mV, Is = 1.2 nA, modulation frequency 613 Hz, and modulation amplitude 50 µV; fit the data to a Dynes function (broadening γ = 0.05 µeV) to obtain a gap Δ = (1.25 ± 0.01) mV and an effective junction temperature T = (1.21 ± 0.02) K.

steps.title: Recover Nb tip after Au coating
steps.instruction: Dip the tip a few dozen nanometres into the Au(111) crystal until the zero‑bias conductance matches the quasiparticle conductance (indicating an Au overlayer > 40 nm). Voltage pulsing to 10 V and mild field emission at 30 V do not restore the gap. Remove the Au layer by Ar⁺ sputtering: use 3 keV ions at 10 µA cm⁻², chamber pressure 1 × 10⁻⁵ mbar, positioning the tip ≈ 4 mm off‑center of the beam. Perform sputtering cycles of 45 min, 45 min, 47 min and 55 min (total 192 min), checking the superconducting gap after each cycle; the sputtering yield is roughly 10 nm h⁻¹.

steps.title: Optimize STM RF filtering using Nb tip
steps.instruction: Record differential conductance spectra before (blue trace) and after (black trace) adding pi‑filters (Tusonix 2499‑003‑X7R0‑101MLF plus 10 kΩ resistor) on the piezo scanners and disconnecting the coarse‑motion walkers; the fully formed SC gap with sharp coherence peaks after filtering indicates successful RF noise reduction.
